meta.description: Executed comprehensive meteorological forecasting and issued timely Watches, Warnings, and Advisories (WWA) to safeguard aviation assets and personnel operating out of Butts Army Heliport.
meta.jhaNotes:
Work Area Hazard Analysis: Meteorological Watch & Outdoor Observation 
Hazard: High noise levels. 
Source: Environmental and operational noise exposure encountered when stepping outside to perform meteorological watch (metwatch) and conducting outdoor observations. Potential for cumulative hearing strain or noise-induced hearing loss with prolonged, unprotected exposure. 
Impact Potential for cumulative hearing strain or noise-induced hearing loss with prolonged, unprotected exposure. 
Mandatory Mitigation / Controls 
Engineering & Administrative Controls: Limit duration of continuous outdoor exposure where operationally feasible. 
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Mandatory use of approved earplugs for all personnel stepping outside to conduct metwatch or outdoor observations.

meta.activeShooterMethods: In an active shooter situation, follow the Run, Hide, Fight protocol. First, if an escape route is available, run immediately, leave your belongings behind, keep your hands visible, and call 911 once safe. If evacuation is impossible, hide by locking and barricading doors, silencing phones, and staying completely out of sight. As an absolute last resort when your life is in imminent danger, fight the attacker aggressively using improvised weapons and teamwork to neutralize the threat.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter: During severe or adverse weather, immediately move to the designated shelter area within the facility, staying away from windows, exterior doors, and large open rooms. Remain inside and low to the ground, keeping emergency communication devices ready, and wait until management or emergency personnel issue an official all-clear before exiting.
meta.fireEquipmentNotes: In the event of an emergency, fire extinguishers on the second floor are located near both front and rear exits, while first-floor extinguishers are positioned at every exit and inside the armory. Additionally, an emergency eyewash station is located on the first floor near the armory and the garage door. Finally, the AED's are located first floor near the armory and second floor in the rightmost kitchen cabinet.

Local Rider Briefing & Area Hazards (Colorado Springs / Local Installations): 

Local Hazards & Environmental Conditions: Mountain driving risks including loose gravel, potholes, rapid weather changes (rain, hail, extreme temperature shifts), high winds, and local wildlife hazards (deer, elk, bears). 

Mandatory Briefings & Tracking: Complete Initial Commander/MSR Safety Briefing, annual Preseason Kickoff Briefing, and maintain an active account in MUSTT/AFSAS per DAFI 91-207. Repeat briefing upon PCS or commander changes. 

Training Cadence: Initial training required prior to operating; Intermediate training within 60 days to 1 year; Refresher training required every 5 years. 

Mandatory PPE (On/Off Duty & On/Off Base): DOT/Snell/UNECE certified helmet fastened under the chin; ANSI Z87.1 approved eye protection or full-face shield; long-sleeved shirt/jacket; long trousers; full-fingered leather or abrasion-resistant gloves; over-the-ankle sturdy footwear.

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: Laser Safety Training
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide laser hazard awareness, eyewear, posting, alignment, and beam-control training before personnel work with lasers or enter laser-controlled areas.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local laser safety officer guidance and approved operating instructions to cover exposure limits, alignment procedures, and emergency actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFI 48-139 / Laser and Optical Radiation Protection

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Fetal Protection Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide job-specific hazard awareness for reproductive health risks where occupational exposures may affect pregnant workers or fetuses.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use occupational and environmental health guidance to discuss declaration options, exposure review, and local work restriction procedures.
